brief.headline: Close the ₹8.48 L price gap on PET bottles — we already pay ₹7.62/piece to TPAC for the same 250ml amber bottle

priceAsk.summary: Match the ₹7.62/NOS we pay TPAC for PET BOT AMBER 250ML/28MM — a straight 11.5% cut on that SKU alone
priceAsk.target: ₹7.62/NOS for PET BOT AMBER 250ML/28MM WITH SHR SL 01, saving ₹8.48 L/year across the portfolio
priceAsk.basis: We buy the identical bottle from TPAC Packaging at ₹7.62/NOS; PIK charges us ₹8.49/NOS. TPAC proves the market will do ₹7.62 — PIK needs to match or we shift volume.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Keep 30 Days After Receipt — no change needed

brief.financialLeverage: PIK Plastics publishes no financials, so we don't know their revenue, profit or cash position. Our ₹1.92 Cr annual spend is material for a private converter, and the fact that we're overpaying ₹8.48 L means they have pricing room. We have four strong alternates lined up — including Manjushree (₹2569.83 Cr, India's largest rigid converter) and listed Mold-Tek (₹946.50 Cr, health B) — so we can credibly walk if PIK won't move. Push firmly on price; their lack of transparency means we lean on our own data and on second-source readiness.

evidence.point: We pay PIK ₹8.49/NOS for the 250ml amber PET bottle; TPAC supplies the identical item at ₹7.62/NOS
Closing the price gap on that one SKU saves us ₹7.19 L a year
Total estimated overpayment to PIK across all items is ₹8.48 L annually
Our annual spend with PIK is ₹1.92 Cr — enough to matter to a private packaging firm
Market research shows 28mm PP caps typically trade at ₹0.85–0.95/pc, with headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic converter (₹2569.83 Cr revenue, health B 65/100) — pharma bottles, caps and preforms; our top second-source candidate and already a backup for packaging.

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader (₹946.50 Cr revenue, health B 73/100) serving pharma with pails, containers and closures — robust alternate for bottles.

alternates.name: Pearl Polymers Ltd
alternates.why: Listed PET bottle and jar specialist under the Pearlpet brand (₹19.83 Cr revenue) — direct fit for our PET bottles, though smaller and lower health (D 24/100).

risks: PIK publishes no financials, so we can't gauge how hard to push without tipping them into trouble — watch for signs of cash stress if we squeeze too fast.
TPAC's ₹7.62 price sets our benchmark, but confirm TPAC can absorb more volume before we shift — don't create a new single-point-of-failure.
The market-backup leads (Reliance, IVL Dhunseri, Chemco) are unqualified research names — verify and price them before calling them alternates in the room.
If PIK won't move on the 250ml bottle (₹7.19 L of the ₹8.48 L gap), the smaller SKU savings may not justify the effort — prioritise the big-ticket item first.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We're paying you ₹8.49 a bottle for the 250ml amber PET when TPAC does the same piece at ₹7.62 — help us understand why we shouldn't just move that volume to them.
